extracted.intended_audience: Attorneys authorized to practice before the USPTO; respondents and counsel in USPTO reciprocal disciplinary proceedings; OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing imposition of reciprocal suspension by the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including notice/service, response opportunity, limited recognition to conclude matters, publication, account restrictions, and reinstatement conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and Order service and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be sent to the Respondent (here: by certified mail) notifying them that a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline has been filed and providing a response opportunity; if the Notice and Order cannot be delivered, it shall be published in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order in this case was sent by certified mail (receipt nos. provided); because it was not deliverable it was published in the Official Gazette on two consecutive weeks (dates provided). The Notice provided Respondent 40 days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response opportunity and grounds to oppose (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is afforded a 40-day period to file a response opposing imposition of identical reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons listed in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order must explain the specific statutory/regulatory defenses available under § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a timely response may result in the Director determining there is no genuine issue of material fact and imposing identical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination when respondent fails to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Respondent does not file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose the identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter, Respondent did not file a response, and the Director determined reciprocal suspension for 180 days was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and duration of reciprocal suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: When reciprocal discipline is imposed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, the USPTO may suspend the Respondent from practice before the USPTO for the same duration and scope as imposed by the state authority (here: suspended from practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO for 180 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies the suspension applies to trademark and non-patent matters; Respondent was noted as not authorized to practice patent matters prior to this action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to conclude pending matters (37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent may be granted limited recognition for a specified short period (here: thirty (30) days) starting on the date of the Final Order to conclude work on behalf of clients on any matters pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If work cannot be concluded within the limited recognition period, the Respondent must advise each client so the client may make other arrangements. Limited recognition is explicitly tied to § 11.58(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the order's notice of suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order provides a model 'Notice of Suspension' for Official Gazette publication and specifies the FOIA Reading Room URL where disciplinary decisions are publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disabling/suspending USPTO.gov accounts after limited recognition expires
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective upon expiration of the 30-day limited recognition, the USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to the Respondent (including all accounts Respondent has ever established, sponsored, or used in connection with trademark or patent matters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This authority is discretionary ('authorized to disable or suspend'). The order lists account types and notes it applies when the limited recognition period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining/using USPTO verified Electronic System accounts during suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have their name added to a USPTO verified Electronic System account, nor may they use, assist others in using, or access any USPTO.gov account(s) for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order explicitly prohibits applying for or attempting to apply for accounts, verifying other persons' credentials, sponsoring accounts, and other actions enumerated in paragraphs 6–8 and 8(1)–(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed prohibitions while suspended (account-related actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a petition for reinstatement is granted under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, Respondent is prohibited from: (1) opening or activating any USPTO.gov account(s) to prepare/file documents; (2) applying for or attempting to apply for any such accounts; (3) verifying or attempting to verify any other person's credentials for USPTO.gov accounts; and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor USPTO.gov accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prohibitions persist until formal reinstatement under § 11.60 and are actionable by the USPTO (the Office is authorized to disallow such actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactivation of disabled/suspended accounts is respondent's responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO is not obligated to sua sponte re-activate any USPTO.gov account disabled or suspended pursuant to the order; it is the Respondent's sole responsibility to initiate re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order clarifies that reactivation is not automatic and places the burden on Respondent after the suspension period or after satisfying reinstatement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and statutory basis for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to statutory and regulatory authority (cited here: 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order states the action is taken under these authorities and indicates disciplinary decisions are made available publicly via OED's FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct predicates and related professional rule violations
rubrics_metrics.description: The reciprocal discipline here was predicated upon suspension by a state court following findings/admissions of violations of Florida Rules Regulating The Florida Bar: 3-7.1(f) (Notice to Law Firms); 4-1.2(c) (Limitation of Objectives and Scope of Representation); 4-1.3 (Diligence); 4-1.4 (Communication); and a finding of violation of 4-8.4(c) (Misconduct Involving Dishonesty, Fraud, Deceit, or Misrepresentation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order summarizes underlying facts: failure to advise of limited scope, failure to communicate after personal falling out, failure to act with reasonable diligence, and providing misleading information about case status — these types of conduct supported the state suspension and formed the basis for reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service and means of notice to parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders must include a certificate of service describing how the order was served (e.g., via first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, and via email to OED Director/counsel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order lists the specific addresses/methods used in this case and certifies transmission to parties; adherence to service methods supports the procedural validity of the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal effect and implementation steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The order specifies effective dates and sequential operational steps: limited recognition period starts on the date of the Final Order (30 days), suspension duration (180 days), account disabling effective upon expiration of limited recognition, and prohibitions continue until reinstatement under § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity about timing ensures Respondent and USPTO understand when limited recognition ends and when broader prohibitions/technical actions (account suspension) may be implemented.
